rounds.text: Virgo Global Ltd trades at a steep price-to-book ratio of 7.50x despite its underlying book value resting at a meager ₹ 0.54 per share [E1]. The company generates negative earnings, reflected by a loss-making P/E of -11.23x that stands in stark contrast to the sector benchmark of 22.3x [E5]. Compounded sales growth has experienced a catastrophic collapse across every recent timeframe, plunging by -41% over five years, -72% over three years, and hitting -79% over the trailing twelve months [E14, E15, E16]. This precipitous top-line contraction is further underscored by official filings explicitly flagging poor sales growth of -41.2% over the past five years [E47]. Compounded share price growth has simultaneously stagnated at -27% over both one and three-year periods, offering zero dividend yield to compensate investors for these severe headwinds [E3, E19, E20]. Conceded: the company displays a screen reason for profit growth greater than 20% year-over-year [E52].
